components.gap: Preserve the identified source variants of thm:p15-stirling-with-remainder and supply the full Feller treatment it promises (Feller I, 3rd ed., held PDF): (a) Feller's justification of the comparison quantity in the II.9 proof: the double inequality (9.5) suggests comparing log n! with a quantity close to the arithmetic mean of its extreme members, the simplest such quantity being (n+1/2)log n - n, which is why d_n of (9.6) is estimated (pp. 52-53); the annex retains (9.5) (annex lines 114-122) and then defines d_n 'as in Feller' (lines 123-126) without this step. (b) Feller's stated justification of the constant determination: the proof that e^C = sqrt(2 pi) is elementary and independent of the material of his chapters IV-VI, and it is postponed to VII.2 because it is naturally connected with the normal approximation theorem (p. 53); the route says only that the constant is determined by Feller's probability-mass argument without a normal-limit theorem (body lines 115-119, annex lines 171-173, w02c-p15-011 body lines 135-142). (c) Narrowed variant: the annex calls its estimate 'the central-ratio argument in the cited VII.2 passage' (annex lines 188-198) but states it only for k <= M sqrt(n) with M fixed, and (2.7) only on bounded x (lines 199-207); Feller's VII.2 states the central-ratio approximation (2.5) a_k ~ a_0 e^{-k^2/nu}, with error less than k^3/nu^2, for every range 0 < k < K_nu with K_nu^3/nu^2 -> 0 (2.4), and says the basic relation (2.7) a_k ~ h n(kh) is valid when nu -> infinity and k < K_nu satisfies (2.4), its use for k of order sqrt(nu) being the special case in which (2.4) is trivially satisfied (pp. 180-181).

Preserve the identified source variants of thm:p15-stirling-worked-boundaries: supply Feller's normative claim that, although the difference of the two sides of (9.1) increases over all bounds, it is the percentage error which really matters (Feller I, 3rd ed., p. 52). The route reports only that Feller separates the two notions of error (w02c-p15-011 body lines 88-92), proves the absolute-error divergence (body lines 316-318, annex lines 695-708) and adds a caution that a small percentage error is not a small absolute error (w02c-p15-011 body lines 149-159); Feller's judgment itself is absent.

Supply the full treatment promised by def:p15-stirling-continuation: its statement that the chapter includes Feller's II.9 Stirling proof (body lines 343-345) is not yet met while the II.9 items listed for C004 are unsupplied: Feller's (9.5)-to-d_n justification of the comparison quantity (pp. 52-53) and his statement that the proof of e^C = sqrt(2 pi) is elementary, independent of his chapters IV-VI and placed in VII.2 because it is naturally connected with the normal approximation theorem (p. 53).

route.locators_checked: Durrett pp. 113-115 (two locators: p. 114 Lemma 3.1.1/Theorem 3.1.2; p. 115 Theorem 3.1.3, Exercises 3.1.1-3.1.4); Feller pp. 52-54 (II.9), VI.3 p. 151 ((3.4)-(3.6)), VII.1 pp. 175, 179 (Lemma 2 and proof), VII.2 p. 180 footnote 3 and pp. 179-181; all show the cited content

defect_observations: Not judged as required items (lead may decide): Feller's evaluative remarks that Stirling's formula is 'an important tool of analytical probability theory' and 'invaluable for many theoretical purposes' (p. 52) and that (9.15) 'supplements Stirling's formula in a remarkable manner' (p. 54); the transitional justifications in the selected VI.3 passage ('less interesting' than at least r successes; an upper bound useful 'even though more sophisticated estimates will be found in the next chapter', p. 151) and before VII.1 Lemma 2 ('convenient to have an elementary estimate of the tail', p. 175); none appears on the route.

VII.2 material outside the selected constant-determination argument, not judged: the two stated reasons for treating p = 1/2 separately and the remark that the proof needs nothing after III.2 (p. 179); the remarks after (2.10) that it extends to some endpoints varying with n, that III (2.7) is contained in it, and that it is a special case of the next section's theorem (p. 181). The VII.1 Note on Terminology (p. 179, incl. the remark that the 'Gaussian' law was used earlier by de Moivre and Laplace) and VI.3's central-term theorem, 'most probable number' caution and 100-tosses example (p. 151) lie outside the selected Lemma 2 and tail-estimate components.

Durrett's reading of S_n as the winnings at time n of $1 bets on a fair coin (p. 113) is not stated in this chapter; the same betting reading of the fair-sign walk is on the route at reflection-and-ballot-counts.tex lines 362-364 (attributed to Durrett p. 265), without a cross-reference from def:p15-stirling-models.

Feller's printed constant in 'an error of less than ... n^{-2} per cent' (p. 54) is overwritten by a handwritten mark in the held scan; w02c-p15-011 body lines 116-121 say so, report the claim as 'of order n^{-2} per cent', and prove the stronger 0.70 n^{-2} per cent bound (item 3, annex lines 84-102) and the 100/(12n^2) per cent reading. Treated as covered in substance.

Feller's (8.11) is valid for -1 < t < 1 (p. 51); thm:p15-stirling-log-tools states the series only for 0 < y < 1, which is the range the II.9 proof uses. The lemma does not attribute the series to Feller.

If Feller's p. 53 claim that the constant proof is independent of chapters IV-VI is added, note that his VII.2 footnote 3 (p. 180) uses the tail estimate VI (3.5), as the handbook's argument does (annex lines 222-230); correctness/fidelity note only.

Body line 40 asserts the 'previously proved Gaussian integral' without a cross-reference; the result is thm:p15-normal-normalization (convolution-gamma-normal.tex line 301).
